A_general.open_code_note: Dovetail describes the public repository as its self-hosted STDIO server, while the input is the hosted Streamable HTTP endpoint. It is the same product and a local server variant, but the hosted documentation lists many tools absent from the code. The code contains eight tools; four are also in the hosted list and four are absent there.
A_general.mcp_protocol_version: NOT FOUND for the hosted endpoint; the SDK dependency is @modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1.12.1 in the local variant.
other_official_servers: The vendor documents a self-hosted STDIO server at https://developers.dovetail.com/docs/mcp-self-hosted; it uses the same product API but has a smaller, different tool set than the hosted endpoint.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: No separate MCP price or MCP-specific plan entitlement was found. The hosted docs describe API-token and browser OAuth access; users need a Dovetail account and API token for token-based access.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: The vendor pricing page lists Free at $0 per user/month and Enterprise at custom pricing. No numeric price for other plans was available in the collected page.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: The pricing page presents a free tier and custom-priced Enterprise. It does not specify an MCP charge, per-call cost, or MCP usage quota.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: The hosted endpoint requires authentication. Hosted OAuth does not support Dynamic Client Registration (DCR) or Client-Initiated Metadata Discovery (CIMD); API-token authentication is offered as an alternative. Dovetail says MCP access follows the connected user's existing Dovetail permissions. The help page also describes enabling a connector through Connected apps.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor and Dovetail workspace permissions; users can connect or disconnect the assistant.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Hosted list includes read and write operations; no readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, or openWorldHint annotations are published. Local tools use server.tool without explicit annotations. 2. No enforced confirmation parameter or preview-confirm flow was found; docs do not describe MCP elicitation or approval gates. 3. OAuth/API-token authentication; Dovetail states access and changes use the connected user's permissions. The metadata lists broad scopes, including write and delete scopes; docs say DCR/CIMD are unsupported. Token lifetime and client allowlists were not found. 4. No hosted read-only mode, tool filter, query-free mode, or environment-specific endpoint was documented. Public code is STDIO and differs in tool set. 5. Vendor says the AI cannot see data the user lacks permission to access. No MCP-specific PII masking rule was found. 6. Hosted rate limits and quotas were not found in the collected MCP docs. Local schemas use pagination limits described as 0-100; hosted file upload docs state up to 5 GB. Local code retries selected network/5xx failures up to three times; hosted server limits remain unknown. 7. Local schemas validate with Zod and construct selected API query parameters; no alias rewriting or operator-argument override was observed. Hosted validation behavior is not documented. 8. Local API calls add source=dovetail-mcp-v1 and User-Agent dovetail-mcp/0.2.0 (stdio); retry messages go to stderr. The vendor says changes are performed on the user's behalf. Hosted MCP audit logging and telemetry details were not found. 9. No feedback/rating/report tool appears in the official hosted list or local code. The help page invites users to share feedback with the Dovetail team outside the tool list. No tool-result upsell was found. 10. No server-provided AI skill or behavioral tool instruction was found. Vendor help contains general use/setup descriptions; the local code has no initialize instructions. 11. No MCP memory/state mechanism was found in the docs or local code. 12. Hosted HTTP and self-hosted STDIO variants have different tool sets; see A_general. No nested vendor agent or proxy architecture was documented. 13. No raw API request, arbitrary SQL, or script execution tool appears in the hosted list or local code.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: Dovetail documents a hosted Streamable HTTP endpoint and a separate self-hosted STDIO variant with a different, smaller tool set.

No catalogue-only tools were added. The Claude connector directory lists nine names, all matching the official hosted list or official local code. Glama reports seven local-code tools; APIs.io and Manufact report nine tool names in their collected pages. These catalogue counts describe their observed snapshots, not a stated vendor total.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: No behavioral instruction to the AI was found in the hosted tool descriptions, which are short operation summaries. Setup guidance is addressed to the user/client and includes: “Your MCP client must support setting a custom Authorization header to pass a Dovetail API token.” No server enforcement of that client guidance was established.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Dovetail states: “The AI only has access to the information you can access. It can’t see projects or data that you don’t have permission to access. Any changes made through the MCP server are performed on your behalf, using your own access and permissions.” The privacy policy says Dovetail excludes training generalized/non-personalized AI and ML models from stated service-improvement use. No MCP-specific retention or masking rule was found.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The help page says users can connect or disconnect the assistant whenever they like. The developer documentation describes OAuth browser authentication and API-token setup.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Permission inheritance is documented as a product promise; the hosted implementation is closed, so its enforcement could not be inspected. The local code sends an API token to the Dovetail API, but does not demonstrate hosted OAuth permission enforcement. The privacy statement concerns Dovetail's general service-improvement use, not a specifically documented MCP data path.

contradictions: The hosted developer page says the endpoint handles OAuth 2.1 or API tokens, while its hosted-endpoint section also says custom clients must pass an API token and that DCR/CIMD are unsupported. The supplied protected-resource and authorization-server metadata documents an authorization-code and refresh-token flow, so the OAuth flow is discoverable but third-party client registration is constrained.

The protected-resource metadata advertises delete scopes for channels, comments, contacts, fields, folders, insights, notes, and projects, while the official hosted tool list contains no corresponding delete tools. Scopes do not establish that those operations are exposed through MCP.
The official hosted tool list contains 50 tools; the public local STDIO code has eight tools, four not listed in the hosted tool list. Tool surfaces therefore differ between vendor variants.

The vendor help page describes the server as supporting creation of projects, docs, data, highlights, and channel data; the public local code implements only read-oriented retrieval tools. This aligns with the distinction between hosted and self-hosted variants rather than proving a hosted mismatch.
observations_for_research: The hosted OAuth resource metadata exposes substantially broader scopes, including delete and chat scopes, than the published MCP tool list exposes as named operations.
The vendor provides both browser OAuth and API-token setup for the hosted endpoint, while disallowing DCR and CIMD for third-party clients.

The hosted tool list combines retrieval with content creation, uploads, and imports; the public local variant offers a smaller read-focused interface and includes legacy insight-listing tools absent from the hosted list.
The same user-permission boundary is stated for hosted MCP operations, while the public code demonstrates bearer-token forwarding to the product API.
